title: 5.7.19 Collectible Class
description: Write a Collectible class, instantiate at least 5, and detect overlap with the player. SLO-2 lab: the class is the point. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Fill in the Collectible constructor
steps.instructions: The class shell is already in the editor: `class Collectible` with an empty `constructor(x, y, value, color)` and an empty `collect()`. Fill in the constructor: store the data on `this` and create `this.sprite = new Sprite(...)`.
hints: Re-read 5.7.11 Worked Example: the `Enemy` constructor follows the same `this.x = x` / `this.sprite = new Sprite(...)` pattern.

steps.title: Add a collect() method
steps.instructions: Add a `collect()` method on the class that despawns the sprite and returns `this.value`.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the moSHion docs drawer for how to despawn a sprite.

steps.title: Instantiate at least 5 Collectibles
steps.instructions: In `setup()` (after the player is created), push at least 5 `new Collectible(...)` into the `collectibles` array at different positions, with different values and colors.
hints: A `for` loop with `collectibles.push(new Collectible(...))` is one option: a `const` per item works too.

steps.title: Detect overlaps and collect
steps.instructions: In `draw()`, iterate the `collectibles` array. When the player overlaps a collectible's sprite (player.overlaps(c.sprite)), call its `collect()` method, add the returned value to `totalScore`, and remove that item from the array.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the moSHion docs drawer for the overlap check.
Removing items while iterating forwards skips neighbours: search for 'iterate backwards to splice' if you hit that bug.

requirements.title: Constructor stores state on the object
requirements.description: The constructor body assigns at least one argument onto this: the class shell is provided, so this checks the part the student writes. Help: 5.6.5 (constructor and its parameters)

requirements.title: Constructor creates the sprite
requirements.description: The constructor creates the sprite this collectible owns. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

requirements.title: collect() method does work
requirements.description: A collect() method that deletes the sprite (via this.sprite.delete() or sprite.remove()) AND then returns something, with the delete before the return so it runs. Help: 5.7.10 (Lab: Cleanup with this.sprite.delete())

requirements.title: At least one instance
requirements.description: At least one Collectible is instantiated. Help: 5.6.4 (The new operator)

requirements.title: Overlap detection
requirements.description: The code checks for overlap between player and a sprite (.overlaps() or .overlapping()).

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.7.19 Collectible Class". The task they were given: The Collectible class shell is given: constructor(x, y, value, color) and collect(), both empty. Fill in the constructor: store the data on this (at least the value) and create this.sprite = new Sprite(...) in the given colour. Write collect() so it deletes the sprite and returns this.value. In setup(), push at least five new Collectible(...) into collectibles at different positions, with different values and colours. In draw(), go through collectibles; when player.overlaps(c.sprite) is true, call c.collect(), add what it returns to totalScore, and remove that item from the array. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. player.overlaps(other) is true on every frame the two touch, and it takes a sprite, so it is given c.sprite (the Collectible's own sprite), not the Collectible object. sprite.delete() (or remove()) takes a sprite off the screen. Code after a return never runs, so in collect() the delete must come before the return. Removing items from an array while looping forward skips the next item; looping backwards, or over a copy, avoids that. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, ternaries or if-chains, semicolons, spacing, quotes, order and helper functions of their own are all fine; only a name the starter's own code already calls or reads has to keep that name. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or a string never runs, so the starter's STEP comments are never the student's work. Wrong ideas to catch: a return placed before the delete (the delete never runs); overlaps given the Collectible itself instead of its sprite; a collect() that returns nothing. Any parameter names, any sprite size or shape, and a for, for...of or backwards loop all count. colliding(...) also detects the touch and counts for the overlap criterion. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old beginner: short sentences and everyday words.

rubric.title: Constructor stores state on the object
rubric.description: The constructor body stores at least one of its arguments on this (the value, x, y or the colour). Missing: nothing is stored on this. Help: 5.6.5 (constructor and its parameters)

rubric.title: Constructor creates the sprite
rubric.description: The constructor creates a new Sprite(...) and stores it as this.sprite. Missing: no sprite, or it is kept in a local variable instead of this.sprite. Help: 5.1.6 (Sprite: new Sprite(x, y, w, h) + .color)

rubric.title: collect() method does work
rubric.description: collect() deletes this.sprite (delete() or remove()) and returns a value (this.value is what step 2 asks), with the delete placed where it actually runs, before the return. Partial: only one of the two, or a delete that sits after the return and never runs. Missing: collect() is still empty. Help: 5.7.10 (Lab: Cleanup with this.sprite.delete())

rubric.title: At least one instance
rubric.description: At least one new Collectible(...) is built. Five or more, pushed into collectibles, is what step 3 asks and is welcome. Missing: no Collectible is ever built. Help: 5.6.4 (The new operator)

rubric.title: Overlap detection
rubric.description: Inside draw() (or a function it calls), the code tests whether the player touches a collectible's sprite: player.overlaps(...) given the sprite, the same test the other way round, overlapping(...), or colliding(...). Partial: the test is given the Collectible object instead of its sprite. Missing: no touch test in draw().
